equation_source.title: Direction-selective motion discrimination by traveling waves in visual cortex
equation_source.context: Generalized Wilson–Cowan excitatory/inhibitory rate equations (1), (2), sigmoid (8). Computational visual-cortex model; not a human whole-brain connectome.

adaptation: Discrete FMA regions replace a spatial continuum. Signed delayed E-to-E graph coupling and finite rectangular stimuli are NeuroLab assumptions; weights, delays and local default parameters are illustrative, not fitted or imported from the paper.
state_units: E and I normalized population activity, dimensionless 0–1; not Hz, BOLD, percent of cells or receptor occupancy
time_units: model milliseconds; illustrative time constants and delays
history: initial state held constant for all t < 0
numerics: CPU f64, deterministic Heun method of steps; grid-aligned delays >= dt; no randomness or post-step clipping
validation: analytic uncoupled exponential oracle, step convergence, causal delay and disconnection tests; no independent biological validation
connectivity: Explicit illustrative branching graph. Its drawn arcs are schematic, not reconstructed axon tracts.
limitations: Homogeneous E/I masses do not represent cellular types, laminae, neurotransmitters or regional specialization. Cerebellum, brainstem, white matter and cavities have no population model in this version. No real-substance effects are connected.
